title: Put a chef's knife back on the magnetic strip, blade flat
instruction: Put the knife back on the knife rack.
context: Restaurant cooks (1.4 million US workers) and food preparation workers (0.9 million) keep their knives on a magnetic strip above the station and put them back after every task. The strip only holds a blade laid flat along it: a knife lying on the board has to be lifted, rolled a quarter turn so the blade stands, and pressed flat onto the strip with the handle off its end; touched by its edge or held by its handle, it falls.
setup: Layout as in the screenshot (x forward from the line between the arm bases, y to the left of the midline, heights from the counter). Grey laminate counter (52 x 80 x 0.3 cm) centred 34 cm out. White glazed tile backsplash (2 x 120 x 50 cm, grey grout lines every 5 cm), its face 52 cm out, running from 40 cm right to 80 cm left. Magnetic knife strip of black anodised aluminium with magnets inside (40 cm long, 3.5 cm tall, 1.6 cm deep) on the backsplash, centred 26 cm up, running from 17.5 to 57.5 cm left; on it hang two knives upright, handles down, at 44 and 52 cm left: steel blades (16 x 3.5 cm, 2 mm thick) crossing the strip and black polymer handles (11 x 2.2 x 2 cm) below it. Maple cutting board (24 x 36 x 2 cm) centred 30 cm out, 16 cm left, with three carrot slices (2.8 cm across, 8 mm thick). On the board lies a chef's knife flat, along y, blade toward the left: black polymer handle (12 x 2.4 x 1.8 cm) centred 30 cm out, 10 cm left, stainless steel blade (20 cm long, 4.5 cm wide, 2 mm thick), 200 g. A folded cotton towel (14 x 10 x 2.4 cm) 44 cm out, 20 cm right; a clear polypropylene deli tub (11 cm across, 8 cm tall) 46 cm out, 8 cm right.
scoring: 0.25 once the knife is lifted 5 cm off the board; 0.5 when the magnet holds it (blade within 4 mm of the strip, its face within about 8 degrees of the wall, at least 4 cm2 of blade over the strip's face); 1.0 when it hangs still with at least 12 cm2 of blade over the strip, laid along it or hung upright. 0 if the knife is never lifted, or is dropped: falls faster than 0.6 m/s (about a 2 cm fall) while neither the gripper nor the strip holds it. Setting it down on the counter or board and picking it up again is allowed.
reset_notes: Lay the knife back flat on the board at its mark, blade toward the strip's end.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, friction 1.2. The knife is a rigid handle with a 2 mm steel blade; the handle is thicker than the blade, so a handle against the strip holds the blade off it. The magnet is a fixed joint formed at the knife's pose of the moment once the blade face is within 4 mm of the strip, flat to it and over at least 4 cm2 of it; a real strip pulls the blade in from a few millimetres. Real trials: a 40 cm magnetic knife strip and a 20 cm chef's knife.
